Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class StoragePileChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.StoragePileChecks
public final class StoragePileChecks extends Object
Storage pile behavior in a live level that does not touch loader-native automation directly: deposits filling partial stacks before empty ones, growth when a pile fills, and settling consolidating, packing, and sorting. Capability/Transfer-API-facing tests stay in each loader's own StoragePileGameTests.

  • Method Details

    • middleRemovalSettlesAndPublishesBothSurvivingPiles

      public static void middleRemovalSettlesAndPublishesBothSurvivingPiles(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: create a permanent three-block Storage pile and use /data merge block to seed sparse glowstone contents in its end blocks and diamonds in its middle block. Place comparators beside both ends and break the middle before another inventory mutation. Seed two full glowstone stacks below, seven diamonds in the middle, and two single glowstone items above. Only seven diamonds drop. The lower pile packs to two slots (signal 2, light 6); the upper pile merges to one slot (signal 1, light 3). The fixture first drains placement ticks, then seeds sparse local slots and makes a pending upper edit in the removal tick, so it specifically checks rescheduling at the new upper base. That same-tick pending-publication assertion is internal; ordinary deposits pack from the base and cannot create this sparse starting layout.

    • depositFillsCompatiblePartialBeforeEmptySlot

      public static void depositFillsCompatiblePartialBeforeEmptySlot(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture seeds 60 stone in local slot 5 and offers eight more; slot 5 reaches 64 and slot 0 receives four.

      To check manually, V-deposit 60 stone into Storage, then eight more in Survival. All eight leave the hand; one full stack and a four-item remainder occupy the pile. The exact pre-settlement slot placement is an internal assertion.

    • fullPileGrowsByOneBlock

      public static void fullPileGrowsByOneBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: allow pile height of at least two, fill all 27 slots of a Storage block with full dirt stacks, and leave replaceable, unobstructed space above. V-deposit one stone. A second Storage block appears and stores it; the hand is emptied in Survival.

    • grownBlockTakesTheBaseFacing

      public static void grownBlockTakesTheBaseFacing(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: build a two-block Storage pile, give its base one redstone-torch turn and its top block three, fill both blocks with full dirt stacks, then V-deposit one stone. The new third block shows the base's layout, not the top block's.

    • settleConsolidatesExactIdentityAndPacksDown

      public static void settleConsolidatesExactIdentityAndPacksDown(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal settlement fixture: directly seed stone stacks of 40 and 30 with {variant:1} and two stacks of five with {variant:2} in separated slots, then settle. Slots 0-2 contain 64, 6, and 10, preserving the two tag identities.

      For a visible check, /give stone with those tags and deposit the same totals into Storage. After settlement, matching tags merge into legal stacks, distinct tags stay separate, and occupied cells pack toward the base. The test's initial gaps require direct fixture writes.

    • extractionSettlesOnScheduledBlockTick

      public static void extractionSettlesOnScheduledBlockTick(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: store one full stone stack and one dirt item in Storage. Plain-right-click the stone cell with an empty hand. The stone enters the hand, and after the scheduled block update the remaining dirt packs into the base slot. The test directly seeds the initial order and waits two ticks.

    • emptyTemporaryPileDisappearsButPermanentPileRemains

      public static void emptyTemporaryPileDisappearsButPermanentPileRemains(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: place two Storage piles with one item each. Select Toggle Permanent, hold V, and empty-hand right-click one pile. Release V and extract the last item from each. After settlement, the temporary pile disappears while the permanent pile remains empty. The automated fixture starts with empty blocks and invokes settlement directly.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholePileFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholePileFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture puts a full stone stack in the lower block of a two-block pile and checks that both blocks return the pile signal.

      To reproduce: create a permanent two-block Storage pile by filling until it grows, then toggling permanence. Extract until only one full stack remains. Put outward-facing comparators beside both blocks on solid supports; both read the same whole-pile fill.

    • ordinaryPlacementBelowPermanentPileRepairsDerivedState

      public static void ordinaryPlacementBelowPermanentPileRepairsDerivedState(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal native-placement check: create a full, permanent Storage block above an empty position with an outward-facing comparator. Its output is 15. Directly place an empty Storage block below it with neighbor updates. After settlement, both blocks remain permanent, contents move into the new base, and the comparator reads 8.

      To reproduce this placement path, prepare the upper pile on a temporary support, fill it, toggle permanence, remove the support, and use /setblock to place somestacks:storage_stack_block below it. Ordinary item deposits do not create the test's empty new base.

    • comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyPile

      public static void comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyPile(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture reads an empty pile, adds one stone, then fills all 27 slots with full stone stacks: signals are 0, 1, and 15.

      To reproduce: make a permanent one-block Storage pile with an outward-facing comparator. Empty it, deposit one stone, then fill it without allowing growth. Read 0, 1, and 15 after updates.
